messages:
Marie (eng-platform): quick sync — we're seeing OTEL ingest costs spike for a few high-throughput routes, thinking we should try a route+tier dynamic head/tail policy.
Jon C: +1. Do you mean per-route head sampling for traces and heavier tail sampling for errory routes?
Marie (eng-platform): exactly. idea: head=always keep first N spans per trace, tail=probabilistic keep for traces with high latency/errors. then apply a route+customer_tier multiplier so enterprise routes keep more.
Ashok R: sounds good. curious about exporter implications — if we drop spans at the collector vs later, we reduce egress cost earlier. but some downstream evals need full traces.
Melissa - Observability: if we drop at collector we lose detail for root-cause on incidents. maybe we can keep full for a small % of high-volume routes and do partial retention otherwise. also dashboards need stable counts — sampling changes will skew alert thresholds.
Marie (eng-platform): agreed. proposal: collector-level sampling with two knobs: head_count (N) and tail_rate (p). policy key = concat(route, ":", customer_tier). default: head_count=3, tail_rate=0.01. enterprise override: head_count=10, tail_rate=0.1.
Jon C: can you sketch config?
Marie (eng-platform): paste config snippet:
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    sampling:
      policy:
        - match: { route: ".*", tier: "standard" }
          head_count: 3
          tail_rate: 0.01
        - match: { route: "^/api/payments.*", tier: "enterprise" }
          head_count: 10
          tail_rate: 0.1
```
This runs in the collector pre-exporter.
Ashok R: Implementation note: collector should tag sampled=false for dropped spans so the exporter can do downstream downsampling metrics and retention reports. also add a metric for "spans_dropped_by_sampling".
otel-ingest-bot: ingestion: received 1.2M spans/min, sampled 92.3% (drops 1.1M), exporter throughput 74K spans/min.
Melissa - Observability: UX questions: how will ops teams change policies? need console page: per-route sampling preview, estimate cost delta, and simulated dashboard impact. also rollout support: canary sampling config to 1% of traffic then ramp.
Jon C: +1 on canary. we should also emit a small retain-set: keep a golden set of full traces for each route for offline evals and regression testing. maybe 0.05% global.
Marie (eng-platform): good call. final open questions: 1) retention window for sampled vs full traces (we're thinking sampled traces 7d, golden/full 30d), 2) how to present sampled counts in Query UI (show estimated totals and sampling factors).
Melissa - Observability: for queries show both raw stored count and estimated original count = stored / effective_sampling_rate. label visualizations with sampling policy and confidence. add a note in alerts docs: when sampling_policy != none, thresholds are advisory.
Ashok R: any perf concerns? head_count adds per-trace state in the collector. need to tune LRU for long-lived traces. maybe enforce a max trace length cutoff and TTL 2s for trace state to bound memory.
Marie (eng-platform): I'll draft a short RFC with config, rollout plan, collector changes, and console mockups. target: alpha deploy to staging next week. comments welcome. :sparkles: 
Jon C: thanks — will review and add a small stress test for the collector LRU.
Melissa - Observability: I'll mock the console preview and cost estimates — want to validate against last 30d of telemetry.
Marie (eng-platform): thanks all. ping me if you want to be on the RFC thread.
